Your public IP is assigned by your Internet provider and is what every website sees. Inside your home or office, devices use private addresses such as 192.168.1.20, 10.0.0.5 or 172.16.0.8. These ranges are reused by millions of networks, so your router translates them to its single public address (NAT). Many mobile and fibre providers add another layer, carrier-grade NAT (100.64.0.0/10), so several customers can share one public IP.
